# MCP directory submissions

Tracks where archy is listed as an MCP server. Every release, refresh the description on every listed directory to match the new version. Treat this file the way you treat `CHANGELOG.md`: it lives or dies with each release.

## Listed

| Directory | URL | Current version | Last verified | State |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Official MCP registry | https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io (`io.github.hslee16/archy`) | 0.46.2 | 2026-09-05 | auto-published on release |
| Glama | https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/hslee16/archy | tracks PyPI | 2026-09-05 | self-updating, no action |
| Smithery | https://smithery.ai/skills/alex-1c6e/archy (Smithery uses "skills" terminology in 2026) | listed | 2026-09-05 | **description stale** |

**Verify a listing by querying it, never by reading this table.** That is the
only method that has found anything here. The official registry sat at 0.13.3
for 33 minor versions while this file, the release checklist and a passing test
all said `server.json` was current, because every one of them checked the FILE
----
  on release via GitHub OIDC (#462), so the entry follows `server.json`, which
  `tests/test_server_json.py` keeps in step with `pyproject.toml` and now also
  checks declares the `mcp` subcommand.
- **Glama** renders the README and a live PyPI version badge, so it tracks
  releases on its own. Nothing to do per release.
- **Smithery**'s description is stale: it says "four-axis quality score" when the
  score has five axes (modularity, acyclicity, depth, equality, complexity). It
  predates the complexity axis. Fixing it needs a login, so it is maintainer-side.

## Pending

| Directory | Submission path | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| mcp.so | https://mcp.so/submit | Form-based; asks for submitter identity, so maintainer-side ([#340](https://github.com/hslee16/archy/issues/340)) |
| PulseMCP | https://www.pulsemcp.com/submit | Form-based; same ([#340](https://github.com/hslee16/archy/issues/340)) |
| `awesome-mcp-servers` | PR to https://github.com/punkpeye/awesome-mcp-servers | One-line entry under the right section ([#324](https://github.com/hslee16/archy/issues/324)) |
| `awesome-claude-code-toolkit` | PR to https://github.com/rohitg00/awesome-claude-code-toolkit | One-line MCP-server entry ([#324](https://github.com/hslee16/archy/issues/324)) |

## Reusable submission kit
----

### Screenshot
`archy render --view dsm` against a real repo (new in v0.42.0): one self-contained HTML page, and the flagged cells show the differentiator faster than a terminal dump of a score. Fall back to `archy_graph` summary output only where a directory rejects HTML-derived images.

### Demo video (60s, optional but Smithery weights it)
A screencap of a Claude-Code session using archy tools to avoid a regression: snapshot at start, edit a load-bearing module, diff at end to see the score drop and the added cycle.

## Per-release refresh checklist

When cutting a new version (Nx.y.z):

- [x] ~~Republish the official registry entry.~~ **Automated.** The `registry`
      job in `publish.yml` publishes `server.json` on every release. Still bump
      both version fields in `server.json`; `tests/test_server_json.py` fails CI
      if you forget. After the release, confirm the LIVE entry moved, because a
      green job is not the same fact as a changed listing.
- [ ] Update `Current version` columns in the table above.
- [ ] Glama: log in, navigate to https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/hslee16/archy, edit metadata to match the new tagline / short description if anything changed.
- [ ] Smithery: same flow at https://smithery.ai/skills/alex-1c6e/archy.
- [ ] mcp.so / PulseMCP / official registry / awesome-mcp-servers / awesome-claude-code-toolkit: only refresh when there is a substantive change (new MCP tool, new core feature). Patch releases skip these.
- [ ] If the bundled skill gained a new MCP tool name, raise the Claude plugin floor (`EXPECTED_SPEC` / shim / README) and extend `TOOL_FIRST_VERSION` in `tests/test_plugin.py` (#668).
- [ ] Update `Last refreshed` to today's date.

## Source

The "submit to every MCP directory" guidance is from the 2026 MCP distribution playbook tracked in the local research notes. The "Smithery uses skills terminology in 2026" detail is confirmed empirically (current archy listing URL pattern).

fix(graph): a PEP 420 namespace monorepo reports "No cycles found" with a real cycle, and nothing points at roots:
open

## Problem

In a PEP 420 namespace-package layout (the shape `uv` workspaces produce: several distributions contributing to one top-level name, no `__init__.py` at the namespace level), archy with **no config** reports a clean result for a graph that has a real cycle, and nothing points the user at `roots:`.

Reproduced on main at v0.50.1. Fixture:

```
packages/core/src/acme/core/{__init__,util,leak}.py   # leak: from acme.web import views
packages/web/src/acme/web/{__init__,views}.py         # views: from acme.core import util, leak
packages/svc/src/svc/{__init__,main}.py
```

`acme.core.leak` and `acme.web.views` import each other.

| Command (no `archy.yaml`) | Output |
|---|---|
| `archy cycles .` | `# No cycles found (min_size=2).` |
| `archy score .` | `graph: 7 modules, 0 edges` |
| `archy graph . --format json` | nodes named `core.util`, `web.views` (the `acme` prefix is lost); every edge targets a phantom `acme` node; zero internal edges |

The cycle exists and is invisible. This is the same class as #516 (decoy root renames the library) and #523 (0 internal modules reports a clean pass): a result that cannot fire looks exactly like a clean codebase (AGENTS.md, "Config and rules").

## The workaround exists, and is easy to get wrong

README "Namespace packages (`roots:`)" documents the fix, but the semantics are the reverse of the PYTHONPATH / Tach `source_roots` / grimp intuition: a root names **the package directory itself**, not the directory containing it.

- `roots: [packages/core/src]` (the intuitive src root): modules are named `src.acme.core.*`. Silently wrong, no warning unless a `layers:` block is also declared.
- `roots: [packages/core/src/acme, packages/web/src/acme, packages/svc/src/svc]`: correct. Names are `acme.core.*`, the cycle appears, and a `forbid: core -> web` fires.

Both runs verified; the second reports `layer coverage: 5 of 5 modules (100%)`.

## Why this is worth doing (anti-theater)

**What changes in action:** a user (or agent) running `cycles` or `score` on such a repo is told, in the same output, "N imports target `acme`, a directory with no `__init__.py` that contains scanned packages (PEP 420 namespace); set `roots:` to the package directories" and fixes the config, instead of trusting a green result. That is a different action, not a different dashboard.

**Evidence and its limit:** the layout is mainstream (uv workspaces are the documented monorepo path; grimp, Tach #192 and Gauge's uv-workspace post all call out namespace packages and multiple source roots as the hard case). I have no archy-measured prevalence and #536 has not run, so this is a correctness fix justified by the false-green, not a claim about adoption. Per the usage baseline, do not size it by downloads.

## Sketch (smallest thing that closes the false green)

1. **Detect, do not infer.** When an import is classified external but its top-level name is a directory under the scan that has no `__init__.py` and contains one or more scanned packages, emit a one-line warning on every surface that reports coverage. Warn, do not guess `roots:`.
2. **Say it where coverage is already said** (#404/#362): extend the existing coverage qualifier rather than adding a new channel, so `cycles`, `score`, `check` and the MCP tools carry it.
3. **Docs:** state the `roots:` direction explicitly with the wrong and right example above, since the wrong one is silent.

Out of scope here, filed separately only if wanted: deriving `roots:` automatically from `[tool.uv.workspace] members`. That is a feature with its own design question (which members, which layout), and the warning in (1) is enough to stop the false green.

## Acceptance (per AGENTS.md)

- Wired to all three surfaces in one change: CLI text, CLI JSON, MCP return model; reason present in every format; asserted on `model_dump()`.
- The fixture above is a test fixture and the test asserts the fixture reaches the branch (an external import whose top-level is a namespace directory) before asserting the warning.
- Mutation-checked: disable the detection and the test goes red; clear `__pycache__` between mutants.
- Negative case: a repo importing a genuine third-party package that happens to share a directory name with nothing scanned must not warn.
- `archy check` / `archy cycles` canary on the repo's own tree still exit 0.

## Related

#516, #523 (same false-green family), #404/#362 (coverage qualifier), #531 (two files mapping to one qualname), #528 (init-less subdirectory in contracts).

"""Did-you-mean hints and name resolution for a module or file the caller mistyped.

archy:owns        hint_unresolved, resolve_modules, suggest_files, suggest_modules
archy:mirrored-by hint_unresolved -> archy.graph, archy.mcp_runs_graph, archy.simulate,
                  resolve_modules -> archy.graph, archy.mcp_runs_graph, archy.simulate,
                  suggest_files -> archy.graph, archy.impact,
                  suggest_modules -> archy.affected, archy.cli_graph,
                  archy.conventions, archy.graph, archy.mcp_runs_graph
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import difflib
from collections.abc import Iterable
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath

import networkx as nx
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict

from archy.graph_models import UnresolvedHint

# Lowest difflib ratio at which `suggest_modules` calls a name a misspelling. A
# one-letter slip in a short dotted name (`archy.scor`) scores ~0.95; two
# unrelated modules sharing a package prefix (`archy.cli`, `archy.dsm`) score
# ~0.67, and must not be offered as the answer to each other.
_SUGGEST_MIN_SIMILARITY = 0.8


# How far below the closest misspelling a candidate may fall and still be offered.
_SUGGEST_MARGIN = 0.1


def suggest_modules(known: Iterable[str], ref: str, limit: int = 5) -> list[str]:
    """Module names `ref` was probably meant to be, best first; `[]` when nothing is close.

    For a lookup that found nothing, to name the near misses in the refusal
    rather than leave the caller to guess again. It suggests and never accepts:
    a bare `cli` would match `archy.cli` and every `tests.*cli*` module, so
    resolving it would pick one of them for the caller.

    Names that contain `ref` come first (`cli` finds `archy.cli`), then names
    spelled like it (`archy.scoer` finds `archy.score`, similarity ratio 20/22).
    Of the misspellings only those within `_SUGGEST_MARGIN` of the closest are
    kept: a clear winner is not diluted by siblings that merely share its
    prefix (`tests.test_dsmm` finds `tests.test_dsm`, not also `tests.test_mcp`).
    Each tier is ordered by name, the second by similarity then name, so the
    answer does not depend on the order `known` arrives in.
    """
    if not ref:
        return []
    names = sorted(set(known))
    contained = [n for n in names if ref in n]
    taken = set(contained)
    scored = []
    for n in names:
        if n in taken:
            continue
        ratio = difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, ref, n).ratio()
        if ratio >= _SUGGEST_MIN_SIMILARITY:
            scored.append((-ratio, n))
    scored.sort()
    closest = -scored[0][0] if scored else 0.0
    kept = [n for r, n in scored if -r >= closest - _SUGGEST_MARGIN]
    return (contained + kept)[:limit]


def hint_unresolved(
    graph: nx.DiGraph, refs: Iterable[str], *, base: Path | None = None
) -> tuple[UnresolvedHint, ...]:
    """A hint for each unresolved reference that has a close match, in input order.

    A `.py` reference is a file path and is answered with file paths
    (`suggest_files`); anything else is a module name and is answered with module
    names. A reference with no close match gets no entry rather than an empty one.
    `base` is what a relative path was meant relative to; see `suggest_files`.
    """
    ordered = list(dict.fromkeys(refs))
    by_file = {h.ref: h for h in suggest_files(graph, ordered, base=base)}
    internal = [n for n, d in graph.nodes(data=True) if not d.get("external")]
    hints = (_hint_for(ref, by_file, internal) for ref in ordered)

    """Raised when a scan discovers more modules than the configured ceiling.

    (the CLI, the MCP tools) can render an actionable message without re-deriving
    them.
    """

            f"larger than a typical project and usually means a vendored, cache, or "
            f"generated directory is being scanned. Add it to `exclude:` in "
            f"archy.yaml, point archy at a narrower path, or raise/disable the limit "
            f"with `max_modules:` in archy.yaml (0 disables)."
        )

    path that claims it, relative to the scan root where possible.

def assemble_graph(
    root: Path,
    modules: list[Module],
    parse_results: dict[str, ParseResult],
) -> nx.DiGraph:
    """Build the import + call graph from already-parsed modules.

    This is the resolution-and-assembly half of `build_graph`, split out so the
    cold path and the cache-backed path (`archy.index.build_graph_cached`) share
    one resolution implementation. Resolution is global (relative imports,
    re-export chains, and alias tables all need the full `parse_results` set), so
    keeping a single code path is what guarantees the cached graph is identical
    to a cold build. `parse_results` is keyed by module qualname; a module with
    no entry (its file vanished between discovery and parse) is dropped here, so
    every caller -- build_graph, build_graph_cached, the mcp watcher -- is safe
    without repeating the guard.
    """
    modules = [m for m in modules if m.qualname in parse_results]
    qualname_set = {m.qualname for m in modules}

    graph: nx.DiGraph = nx.DiGraph()
    _add_module_nodes(graph, modules, parse_results)
    resolver = _Resolver(
        qualname_set=qualname_set,
        reexport_maps=_build_reexport_maps(modules, parse_results, qualname_set),
    )
    parse_errors = _add_import_edges(graph, modules, parse_results, resolver)
    _add_call_edges(graph, modules, parse_results, resolver)

    # Freeze once per edge to preserve the public tuple without copying it per call.
    for _, _, data in graph.edges(data=True):
        if "call_lines" in data:
            data["call_lines"] = tuple(data["call_lines"])

    graph.graph["root"] = str(root)
    graph.graph["relative_paths"] = _relative_paths(root, modules)
    graph.graph["parse_errors"] = tuple(sorted(parse_errors))
    # Graph-level, not per-node: a node attribute would reach every node of
    # `archy graph --format json` for the benefit of one `required:` source.
    entrypoints, entrypoint_errors = derive_entrypoints(
        root,
        guarded=(m.qualname for m in modules if parse_results[m.qualname].has_main_guard),
        modules={m.qualname: m.path for m in modules},
    )
    graph.graph["entrypoints"] = entrypoints
    graph.graph["entrypoint_errors"] = entrypoint_errors
    return graph


def graph_to_dict(graph: nx.DiGraph) -> dict:
    """Serialize a graph to the JSON shape emitted by `archy graph --format json`.

    Per-node `instability` (Martin's `I`), `propagation_cost` (MacCormack
    reverse-reach fraction), and `edit_risk` (geometric-mean composite of
    propagation cost, normalized fan-in, and instability) are attached to
    internal nodes only; external modules have no meaningful values within
    the project. When called on a subgraph (e.g. by `archy_graph_focus`),
    values are computed relative to that subgraph's scope, not the full
    project. For the canonical project-wide propagation cost, read
    `archy score`'s `inputs.propagation_cost`.
    """
    instability = compute_instability(graph)
    _, propagation_cost = compute_propagation_cost(graph)
    edit_risk = compute_edit_risk(graph)
    return {
        "root": graph.graph.get("root"),
        "parse_errors": list(graph.graph.get("parse_errors", ())),
        "nodes": [

                **d,
                **({"instability": instability[n]} if n in instability else {}),
                **({"propagation_cost": propagation_cost[n]} if n in propagation_cost else {}),
                **({"edit_risk": edit_risk[n]} if n in edit_risk else {}),
            }
            for n, d in sorted(graph.nodes(data=True))
        ],
        "edges": [
            {"source": u, "target": v, **d}

"""A PEP 420 namespace monorepo must not report a clean result over a graph it never joined (#586).

`acme.core.leak` and `acme.web.views` import each other, but with no `roots:` the
scan names the modules `core.leak` and `web.views` and every `acme` import
resolves to one external node, so `cycles` said "No cycles found" and `score`
said 1.000. Each surface now names the namespace directory and the `roots:` that
fixes it. Controls cover the cases that must stay silent.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
from click.testing import CliRunner

from archy.cli import main
from archy.cycles import CycleScan
from archy.graph import build_graph
from archy.graph_namespace import find_namespace_gaps
from archy.mcp import create_server
from archy.mcp_runs import run_cycles, run_score
from tests.mcp_helpers import call_tool

NAMESPACE_DIRS = ["packages/core/src/acme", "packages/web/src/acme"]


def _write(root: Path, rel: str, text: str = "") -> None:
    path = root / rel
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(text)


def _uv_workspace(root: Path) -> Path:
    """The ticket's fixture: three distributions, two of them contributing to `acme`."""
    _write(root, "packages/core/src/acme/core/__init__.py")
    _write(root, "packages/core/src/acme/core/util.py", "def f():\n    return 1\n")
    _write(root, "packages/core/src/acme/core/leak.py", "from acme.web import views\n")
    _write(root, "packages/web/src/acme/web/__init__.py")
    _write(root, "packages/web/src/acme/web/views.py", "from acme.core import util, leak\n")
    _write(root, "packages/svc/src/svc/__init__.py")
    _write(root, "packages/svc/src/svc/main.py", "X = 1\n")
    return root


@pytest.fixture
def workspace(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
    project = _uv_workspace(tmp_path)
    # Reach the branch before asserting the verdict: an `acme` import that
    # resolved, or an `acme` directory that gained an `__init__.py`, would make
    # every assertion below vacuous.
    graph = build_graph(project)
    assert graph.nodes["acme"]["external"] is True
    assert any(not graph.nodes[p]["external"] for p in graph.predecessors("acme"))
    assert not list(project.glob("packages/*/src/acme/__init__.py"))
    assert not graph.has_edge("web.views", "core.leak")
    return project


def _cycles_text(project: Path) -> str:
    result = CliRunner().invoke(main, ["cycles", str(project)])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    return result.output


def test_detector_names_the_directories_and_the_packages_in_them(workspace: Path):
    (gap,) = find_namespace_gaps(build_graph(workspace))
    assert gap.name == "acme"
    assert list(gap.directories) == NAMESPACE_DIRS
    assert gap.packages == ("core", "web")
    assert gap.importers == 2  # core.leak and web.views


def test_cycles_text_names_the_gap_and_the_roots_to_set(workspace: Path):
    out = _cycles_text(workspace)
    assert "# warning: 2 modules import `acme`" in out
    assert f"roots: [{', '.join(NAMESPACE_DIRS)}]" in out


def test_cycles_json_carries_the_reason_not_a_bare_empty_list(workspace: Path):
    result = CliRunner().invoke(main, ["cycles", str(workspace), "--format", "json"])
    payload = json.loads(result.stdout)
    assert payload["cycles"] == []
    (gap,) = payload["namespace_gaps"]
    assert gap["name"] == "acme"
    assert gap["directories"] == NAMESPACE_DIRS
    assert "roots:" in gap["reason"]


def test_cycles_strict_still_passes_because_a_gap_is_a_warning(workspace: Path):
    """The ticket asks for a warning; refusing would fail repos that shadow a name on purpose."""
    result = CliRunner().invoke(main, ["cycles", str(workspace), "--strict"])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    assert "# warning:" in result.output


def test_score_text_and_json_carry_the_gap(workspace: Path):
    text = CliRunner().invoke(main, ["score", str(workspace)]).output
    assert text.splitlines()[-1].startswith("# warning: 2 modules import `acme`")
    payload = json.loads(CliRunner().invoke(main, ["score", str(workspace), "--format", "json"]).stdout)
    assert [g["name"] for g in payload["namespace_gaps"]] == ["acme"]


def test_mcp_cycles_returns_the_object_shape_with_the_gap(workspace: Path):
    result = run_cycles(workspace, min_size=2, internal_only=True)
    assert isinstance(result, CycleScan)
    assert result.model_dump()["namespace_gaps"][0]["name"] == "acme"
    wire = call_tool(create_server(), "archy_cycles", {"path": str(workspace)})
    assert "acme" in json.dumps(wire, default=str)


def test_score_payload_model_dump_carries_the_gap(workspace: Path):
    """Assert the serialized form: FastMCP sends model_dump()."""
    payload = run_score(
        workspace, internal_only=True, record=False, strict=False, strict_tolerance=0.02
    ).model_dump()
    assert payload["namespace_gaps"][0]["name"] == "acme"
    assert payload["namespace_gaps"][0]["directories"] == tuple(NAMESPACE_DIRS)


def test_the_advised_roots_make_the_cycle_visible(workspace: Path):
    """Assert the ANSWER: following the advice finds the cycle, and the warning goes away."""
    (workspace / "archy.yaml").write_text(
        "roots:\n" + "".join(f"  - {d}\n" for d in NAMESPACE_DIRS) + "  - packages/svc/src/svc\n"
    )
    out = _cycles_text(workspace)
    assert "1 cycle(s) found" in out
    assert "acme.core.leak" in out and "acme.web.views" in out
    assert "# warning:" not in out


def test_a_regular_package_is_not_a_gap(tmp_path: Path):
    _write(tmp_path, "pkg/__init__.py")

"""A PEP 420 namespace monorepo must not report a clean result over a graph it never joined (#586).

`acme.core.leak` and `acme.web.views` import each other, but with no `roots:` the
scan names the modules `core.leak` and `web.views` and every `acme` import
resolves to one external node, so `cycles` said "No cycles found" and `score`
said 1.000. Each surface now names the namespace directory and the `roots:` that
fixes it. Controls cover the cases that must stay silent.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
from click.testing import CliRunner

from archy.cli import main
from archy.cycles import CycleScan
from archy.graph import build_graph
from archy.graph_namespace import find_namespace_gaps
from archy.mcp import create_server
from archy.mcp_runs import run_cycles, run_score
from tests.mcp_helpers import call_tool

NAMESPACE_DIRS = ["packages/core/src/acme", "packages/web/src/acme"]


def _write(root: Path, rel: str, text: str = "") -> None:
    path = root / rel
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(text)


def _uv_workspace(root: Path) -> Path:
    """The ticket's fixture: three distributions, two of them contributing to `acme`."""
    _write(root, "packages/core/src/acme/core/__init__.py")
    _write(root, "packages/core/src/acme/core/util.py", "def f():\n    return 1\n")
    _write(root, "packages/core/src/acme/core/leak.py", "from acme.web import views\n")
    _write(root, "packages/web/src/acme/web/__init__.py")
    _write(root, "packages/web/src/acme/web/views.py", "from acme.core import util, leak\n")
    _write(root, "packages/svc/src/svc/__init__.py")
    _write(root, "packages/svc/src/svc/main.py", "X = 1\n")
    return root


@pytest.fixture
def workspace(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
    project = _uv_workspace(tmp_path)
    # Reach the branch before asserting the verdict: an `acme` import that
    # resolved, or an `acme` directory that gained an `__init__.py`, would make
    # every assertion below vacuous.
    graph = build_graph(project)
    assert graph.nodes["acme"]["external"] is True
    assert any(not graph.nodes[p]["external"] for p in graph.predecessors("acme"))
    assert not list(project.glob("packages/*/src/acme/__init__.py"))
    assert not graph.has_edge("web.views", "core.leak")
    return project


def _cycles_text(project: Path) -> str:
    result = CliRunner().invoke(main, ["cycles", str(project)])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    return result.output


def test_detector_names_the_directories_and_the_packages_in_them(workspace: Path):
    (gap,) = find_namespace_gaps(build_graph(workspace))
    assert gap.name == "acme"
    assert list(gap.directories) == NAMESPACE_DIRS
    assert gap.packages == ("core", "web")
    assert gap.importers == 2  # core.leak and web.views


def test_cycles_text_names_the_gap_and_the_roots_to_set(workspace: Path):
    out = _cycles_text(workspace)
    assert "# warning: 2 modules import `acme`" in out
    assert f"roots: [{', '.join(NAMESPACE_DIRS)}]" in out


def test_cycles_json_carries_the_reason_not_a_bare_empty_list(workspace: Path):
    result = CliRunner().invoke(main, ["cycles", str(workspace), "--format", "json"])
    payload = json.loads(result.stdout)
    assert payload["cycles"] == []
    (gap,) = payload["namespace_gaps"]
    assert gap["name"] == "acme"
    assert gap["directories"] == NAMESPACE_DIRS
    assert "roots:" in gap["reason"]


def test_cycles_strict_still_passes_because_a_gap_is_a_warning(workspace: Path):
    """The ticket asks for a warning; refusing would fail repos that shadow a name on purpose."""
    result = CliRunner().invoke(main, ["cycles", str(workspace), "--strict"])
    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
    assert "# warning:" in result.output


def test_score_text_and_json_carry_the_gap(workspace: Path):
    text = CliRunner().invoke(main, ["score", str(workspace)]).output
    assert text.splitlines()[-1].startswith("# warning: 2 modules import `acme`")
    payload = json.loads(CliRunner().invoke(main, ["score", str(workspace), "--format", "json"]).stdout)
    assert [g["name"] for g in payload["namespace_gaps"]] == ["acme"]


def test_mcp_cycles_returns_the_object_shape_with_the_gap(workspace: Path):
    result = run_cycles(workspace, min_size=2, internal_only=True)
    assert isinstance(result, CycleScan)
    assert result.model_dump()["namespace_gaps"][0]["name"] == "acme"
    wire = call_tool(create_server(), "archy_cycles", {"path": str(workspace)})
    assert "acme" in json.dumps(wire, default=str)


def test_score_payload_model_dump_carries_the_gap(workspace: Path):

    payload = run_score(

684:**Namespace packages (`roots:`).** archy discovers packages by walking `__init__.py` files. PEP 420 namespace packages (no `__init__.py`) are invisible by default. Declare them as roots so descendants get qualified names:
**Namespace packages (`roots:`).** archy discovers packages by walking `__init__.py` files. PEP 420 namespace packages (no `__init__.py`) are invisible by default. Declare them as roots so descendants get qualified names:

```yaml
roots:
  - app           # `app/main.py` becomes `app.main`
  - src/service   # `src/service/db.py` becomes `service.db`
```

A root names the package directory itself, not the directory that contains it: `src/service` makes `service.db`, while `src` would name `src.service.db`. This is the opposite of how `PYTHONPATH` entries work.

Without `roots:`, a project like `app/libs/db.py` (no `app/__init__.py`) is either skipped entirely or shows up as a top-level `libs.db`, which makes layer rules like `app.libs.**` match nothing.

**Layer presence (`min_layers_present:`).** Forbidding edges *between* layers says nothing about whether the layers exist. A codebase that collapsed four layers into one module satisfies every `forbid` rule by having no cross-layer edges at all, and passes silently. Set a floor to catch that:

```yaml
min_layers_present: 3   # at least 3 of the declared layers must contain a module
```

Empty declared layers are reported either way, because every rule naming one is dead:

```console
#   layers present: 2 of 4 declared; empty: repositories, models
#   FAIL: 2 layer(s) present, min_layers_present is 3
```

Unset by default, so existing configs keep their exit codes. The shape is taken from the Constraint Decay paper ([arxiv:2605.06445](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.06445)), whose architecture verifier pairs a dependency-direction rule with exactly this presence floor ("at least 3 of the 4 canonical layers present as distinct directories"). `bench/fixtures/conduit_clean/` reproduces its three cases.

**It is a backstop, not the main event, and the measurement says so.** Across 50 agent-generated backends, every single one produced all four layer directories: this check never fired once, while the direction check caught every failure. Keep it for the collapsed-into-one-module case it is named for, but if you are deciding where to spend effort in a config, spend it on `forbid` rules.

## What

In a PEP 420 namespace monorepo (uv workspace shape) with no `roots:`, `archy cycles` said "No cycles found" and `archy score` said 1.000 over a graph whose halves were never joined (#586). A detector now runs at graph assembly (`archy.graph_namespace.find_namespace_gaps`): an internal module imports an external name, a directory of that name sits above scanned modules, and it has no `__init__.py`. It stores the gaps on the graph, and `cycles` and `score` report them.

- **CLI text:** a `# warning:` line naming the importers, the packages found, and the exact `roots:` to set (the namespace directories, not their parents).
- **CLI JSON:** `cycles` returns the object shape only when a gap exists (or `--exclude-type-checking` is on), so a bare `[]` never hides it; `score` gains `namespace_gaps`.
- **MCP:** `archy_cycles` returns the `CycleScan` object when a gap exists; `ScorePayload.namespace_gaps` is a regular field, asserted on `model_dump()`.
- **Warning, not failure:** `--strict` still passes. The ticket asks to warn, and a repo can shadow a name on purpose. Roots are never guessed.

Behaviour change to flag: the existing `--exclude-type-checking` object (CLI and MCP) now always carries `"namespace_gaps": []`. Two tests that pinned the exact dict were updated.

"""Pairs, the per-PR cap, A's pair expansion, cutoff calibration and pooling for #587.

Pure logic, no model and no I/O, so the rules in
`docs/research/EMBEDDING_ORACLE_RECALL.md` can be pinned by tests before any
embedding is computed. Every rule below is the pre-registered one; none is tuned.

The labeled item is a PAIR (PR, new function, existing function) for both
generators. A is expanded from #548's clusters; B emits one pair per new function.
Both are capped at K per PR before the cutoff is calibrated, so one PR holding 703
new functions counts for at most K pairs on either side.

archy:owns        K, Member, Pair, calibrate_cutoff, cap_pairs, expand_a_firing, pool_pairs
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections import defaultdict
from collections.abc import Callable, Mapping, Sequence

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, computed_field

K = 10  # pairs kept per PR, per generator (pre-registered)


class Member(BaseModel):
    """One function of a cluster, as the ledger and a re-parse together describe it."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    path: str
    qualname: str
    is_new: bool
    nodes: int
    shape: str


class Pair(BaseModel):
    """A (PR, new function, existing function) pair and which generators emitted it."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    pr: str
    repo: str
    new_path: str
    new_qualname: str
    new_nodes: int
    new_shape: str
    existing_path: str
    existing_qualname: str
    existing_shape: str
    similarity: float | None = None
    generators: tuple[str, ...]

    # computed_field, not @property: a payload dump drops a plain property.
    @computed_field  # type: ignore[prop-decorator]
    @property
    def pair_id(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.pr}|{self.new_qualname}|{self.existing_qualname}"

    @computed_field  # type: ignore[prop-decorator]
    @property
    def unit_id(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.pr}|{self.new_qualname}"

    @computed_field  # type: ignore[prop-decorator]
    @property
    def exact_tier(self) -> bool:
        """Shape-identical by archy's own hasher, whatever either generator emitted."""
        return self.new_shape == self.existing_shape


def cap_pairs(pairs: Sequence[Pair], k: int = K) -> list[Pair]:
    """At most `k` pairs per PR, keeping the largest new functions.

    Ties break on the new function's path then qualified name, so the answer does
    not depend on the order the pairs arrive in.
    """
    by_pr: dict[str, list[Pair]] = defaultdict(list)
    for p in pairs:
        by_pr[p.pr].append(p)
    kept: list[Pair] = []
    for pr in sorted(by_pr):
        ranked = sorted(by_pr[pr], key=lambda p: (-p.new_nodes, p.new_path, p.new_qualname))
        kept.extend(ranked[:k])
    return kept


def expand_a_firing(
    pr: str,
    repo: str,
    members: Sequence[Member],
    *,
    overlap: Callable[[Member, Member], float],
    exists_at_both: Callable[[Member], bool],
) -> tuple[list[Pair], int]:
    """One pair per new member, each with its best existing partner in the cluster.

    The partner is the existing member that exists at base AND head with the highest
    `overlap` with the new function; ties go to the smaller (path, qualname). A new
    member with no such partner is dropped, and the count of drops is returned so the
    caller reports it instead of scoring it clean.
    """
    old = [m for m in members if not m.is_new and exists_at_both(m)]
    pairs: list[Pair] = []
    dropped = 0
    for new in (m for m in members if m.is_new):
        if not old:
            dropped += 1
            continue
        partner = min(old, key=lambda o: (-overlap(new, o), o.path, o.qualname))
        pairs.append(_pair(pr, repo, new, partner, generators=("A",)))
    return pairs, dropped


def _pair(
    pr: str,
    repo: str,
    new: Member,
    old: Member,
    *,
    generators: tuple[str, ...],
    similarity: float | None = None,
) -> Pair:
    return Pair(
        pr=pr,
        repo=repo,
        new_path=new.path,
        new_qualname=new.qualname,
        new_nodes=new.nodes,
        new_shape=new.shape,
        existing_path=old.path,
        existing_qualname=old.qualname,
        existing_shape=old.shape,
        similarity=similarity,
        generators=generators,
    )


def calibrate_cutoff(scores: Mapping[str, Sequence[float]], target: float, k: int = K) -> float:
    """The largest observed similarity whose mean capped B count per PR meets `target`.

    `scores` maps every PR of the calibration subset to the top-1 similarity of each
    eligible new function in it (a PR with none maps to `[]`, so it counts as zero).
    Pairs tied at the cutoff are all included, and a PR contributes at most `k`. When
    no observed similarity reaches the target the lowest one is returned, which keeps
    every candidate; the caller records that this happened.
    """
    if not scores:
        raise ValueError("calibration subset is empty; there is no volume to match")
    observed = sorted({s for per_pr in scores.values() for s in per_pr}, reverse=True)
    if not observed:
        raise ValueError("calibration subset has no scored function; the cutoff is undefined")
    for t in observed:
        mean = sum(min(k, sum(s >= t for s in per_pr)) for per_pr in scores.values()) / len(scores)
        if mean >= target:
            return t
    return observed[-1]


def pool_pairs(a_pairs: Sequence[Pair], b_pairs: Sequence[Pair]) -> list[Pair]:
    """The union of A's and B's pairs, one entry per pair id, sorted by id.

    A pair both generators emit is one entry tagged with both, carrying B's
    similarity, so it is labeled once and is blind to which generator found it.
    """
    merged: dict[str, Pair] = {}
    for p in [*a_pairs, *b_pairs]:
        seen = merged.get(p.pair_id)
        if seen is None:
            merged[p.pair_id] = p
            continue
        tags = tuple(sorted(set(seen.generators) | set(p.generators)))
        sim = seen.similarity if seen.similarity is not None else p.similarity
        merged[p.pair_id] = seen.model_copy(update={"generators": tags, "similarity": sim})
    return [merged[i] for i in sorted(merged)]

The rules are the ones in `docs/research/EMBEDDING_ORACLE_RECALL.md`, each in one
small function so a boundary cannot drift:

- A pair is TRUE only if BOTH labelers say TRUE (strict); either labeler's UNSCORABLE
  drops it, never scores it FALSE.
- A (PR, new function) unit is TRUE if any labeled pair for it is TRUE; found by A or B
  by which generator emitted a TRUE pair; only by B if found by B and not by A.
- The headline share drops exact-tier pairs BEFORE units are formed.
- B precision is over all labeled B pairs; its interval is a bootstrap clustered by PR.
- A bar is applied to the point estimate only when its interval does not straddle it;
  otherwise the verdict is null.

Recall here is relative to the pooled set, never absolute.

archy:owns        PASS_PRECISION, Share, Verdict, b_precision, resolve_labels, share, verdict, wilson
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import random
from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict

from bench.embedding_oracle_pairs import Pair

PASS_PRECISION = 0.60
KILL_PRECISION = 0.40
PASS_SHARE = 0.30
KILL_SHARE = 0.10
MIN_B_SCORABLE = 30
MIN_B_REPOS = 10
MIN_TRUE_UNITS = 40
MIN_TRUE_REPOS = 15
MIN_TRUE_PRS = 20
BOOTSTRAP_RESAMPLES = 2000
BOOTSTRAP_SEED = 587
Z95 = 1.959963984540054


def resolve_labels(a: Mapping[str, str], b: Mapping[str, str]) -> dict[str, bool]:
    """Strict truth per pair id: both TRUE. A pair either labeler calls UNSCORABLE is absent.

    The labelers must have seen the same pairs; a mismatch is a refusal, since a pair one
    of them never saw would otherwise be silently scored as the other's answer.
    """
    if set(a) != set(b):
        raise ValueError(f"labelers saw different pairs: {len(set(a) ^ set(b))} ids differ")
    out: dict[str, bool] = {}
    for pid in sorted(a):
        if "UNSCORABLE" in (a[pid], b[pid]):
            continue
        out[pid] = a[pid] == "TRUE" and b[pid] == "TRUE"
    return out


def wilson(k: int, n: int) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """Wilson 95% interval for k of n; the whole unit interval when n is 0."""
    if n == 0:
        return 0.0, 1.0
    p = k / n
    denom = 1 + Z95**2 / n
    centre = (p + Z95**2 / (2 * n)) / denom
    half = Z95 * math.sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + Z95**2 / (4 * n**2)) / denom
    return max(0.0, centre - half), min(1.0, centre + half)


class Share(BaseModel):
    """The headline: how much of the strict TRUE pool only B found (exact-tier excluded)."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    true_units: int
    only_b: int
    only_a: int
    both: int
    repos: int
    prs: int
    measurable: bool
    point: float | None
    low: float | None
    high: float | None


def share(pairs: Sequence[Pair], truth: Mapping[str, bool]) -> Share:
    """Units from labeled, non-exact pairs; the floors decide whether the share is measurable."""
    labeled = [p for p in pairs if p.pair_id in truth and not p.exact_tier]
    units: dict[str, dict[str, set[str]]] = {}
    for p in labeled:
        if truth[p.pair_id]:
            slot = units.setdefault(p.unit_id, {"gens": set(), "repos": set(), "prs": set()})
            slot["gens"].update(p.generators)
            slot["repos"].add(p.repo)
            slot["prs"].add(p.pr)
    only_b = sum(s["gens"] == {"B"} for s in units.values())
    only_a = sum(s["gens"] == {"A"} for s in units.values())
    n = len(units)
    repos = len({r for s in units.values() for r in s["repos"]})
    prs = len({r for s in units.values() for r in s["prs"]})
    measurable = n >= MIN_TRUE_UNITS and repos >= MIN_TRUE_REPOS and prs >= MIN_TRUE_PRS
    low, high = wilson(only_b, n) if n else (None, None)
    return Share(
        true_units=n,
        only_b=only_b,
        only_a=only_a,
        both=n - only_b - only_a,
        repos=repos,
        prs=prs,
        measurable=measurable,
        point=only_b / n if n else None,
        low=low,
        high=high,
    )


class BPrecision(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    scorable: int
    repos: int
    true: int
    point: float | None
    low: float | None
    high: float | None


def b_precision(pairs: Sequence[Pair], truth: Mapping[str, bool]) -> BPrecision:
    """Precision over every labeled B pair (exact tier included), with a PR-clustered interval."""
    scored = [p for p in pairs if "B" in p.generators and p.pair_id in truth]
    clusters: dict[str, list[bool]] = {}
    for p in scored:
        clusters.setdefault(p.pr, []).append(truth[p.pair_id])
    n = len(scored)
    k = sum(truth[p.pair_id] for p in scored)
    low, high = _cluster_bootstrap(list(clusters.values()))
    return BPrecision(
        scorable=n,
        repos=len({p.repo for p in scored}),
        true=k,
        point=k / n if n else None,
        low=low,
        high=high,
    )


def _cluster_bootstrap(clusters: Sequence[Sequence[bool]]) -> tuple[float | None, float | None]:
    """Percentile interval of precision, resampling whole PRs with a fixed seed."""
    if not clusters:
        return None, None
    rng = random.Random(BOOTSTRAP_SEED)
    stats: list[float] = []
    for _ in range(BOOTSTRAP_RESAMPLES):
        draw = [clusters[rng.randrange(len(clusters))] for _ in clusters]
        total = sum(len(c) for c in draw)
        if total:
            stats.append(sum(sum(c) for c in draw) / total)
    stats.sort()
    return stats[int(0.025 * len(stats))], stats[min(len(stats) - 1, int(0.975 * len(stats)))]


class Verdict(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    outcome: str  # pass | kill | null | not_measurable
    reason: str


def verdict(prec: BPrecision, headline: Share) -> Verdict:
    """The pre-registered rule.

    Not measurable below B's scorable floor. A precision kill or pass stands whether or
    not the share is measurable. A bar is applied only when the interval does not
    straddle it; a straddle is null. Pass needs both bars, so an unmeasurable share can
    never pass, and kill is either bar.
    """
    if prec.scorable < MIN_B_SCORABLE or prec.repos < MIN_B_REPOS:
        return Verdict(
            outcome="not_measurable",
            reason=f"{prec.scorable} scorable B pairs from {prec.repos} repos; "
            f"need {MIN_B_SCORABLE} from {MIN_B_REPOS}",
        )
    assert prec.point is not None and prec.low is not None and prec.high is not None
    if prec.point < KILL_PRECISION:
        if prec.high < KILL_PRECISION:
            return Verdict(outcome="kill", reason=f"B precision {prec.point:.3f} < 0.40")
        return Verdict(outcome="null", reason="B precision below 0.40 but its interval straddles it")
    if headline.measurable:
        assert headline.point is not None and headline.low is not None
        assert headline.high is not None
        if headline.point < KILL_SHARE:
            if headline.high < KILL_SHARE:
                return Verdict(outcome="kill", reason=f"only-by-B share {headline.point:.3f} < 0.10")
            return Verdict(outcome="null", reason="share below 0.10 but its interval straddles it")
        if (
            prec.point >= PASS_PRECISION
            and prec.low >= PASS_PRECISION
            and headline.point >= PASS_SHARE
            and headline.low >= PASS_SHARE
        ):
            return Verdict(outcome="pass", reason="precision and only-by-B share clear their bars")
        return Verdict(outcome="null", reason="between the bars, or an interval straddles one")
    return Verdict(
        outcome="not_measurable",
        reason="B precision is not a kill but the TRUE pool is below its floor, so no pass "
        "or share verdict is declared",
    )

"""Pairs, the per-PR cap, A's expansion, cutoff calibration and pooling for #587.

Every expected value is worked by hand in the test, never taken from the code under
test. Each test asserts its fixture reaches the branch before asserting the outcome.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import random

import pytest

from bench.embedding_oracle_pairs import (
    K,
    Member,
    Pair,
    calibrate_cutoff,
    cap_pairs,
    expand_a_firing,
    pool_pairs,
)


def member(qual: str, *, new: bool, nodes: int = 40, path: str | None = None, shape="s") -> Member:
    return Member(
        path=path or f"{qual.replace('.', '/')}.py",
        qualname=qual,
        is_new=new,
        nodes=nodes,
        shape=shape,
    )


def pair(pr="1", new="n.f", old="o.f", *, nodes=40, path=None, gens=("A",), sim=None, **kw) -> Pair:
    return Pair(
        pr=pr,
        repo=kw.get("repo", "r/x"),
        new_path=path or f"{new.replace('.', '/')}.py",
        new_qualname=new,
        new_nodes=nodes,
        new_shape=kw.get("new_shape", "a"),
        existing_path=f"{old.replace('.', '/')}.py",
        existing_qualname=old,
        existing_shape=kw.get("old_shape", "b"),
        similarity=sim,
        generators=gens,
    )


def test_pair_model_dump_carries_the_computed_ids_and_exact_tier():
    """Assert the serialized form: a plain property would be dropped."""
    p = pair(pr="7", new="a.f", old="b.g", new_shape="x", old_shape="x").model_dump()
    assert p["pair_id"] == "7|a.f|b.g"
    assert p["unit_id"] == "7|a.f"
    assert p["exact_tier"] is True
    assert pair(new_shape="x", old_shape="y").exact_tier is False


def test_cap_keeps_the_largest_new_functions_per_pr_and_leaves_small_prs_alone():
    big = [pair(pr="big", new=f"n.f{i}", nodes=30 + i) for i in range(12)]
    small = [pair(pr="small", new=f"n.g{i}", nodes=31) for i in range(3)]
    assert len(big) > K and len(small) < K  # the cap binds on one PR and not the other
    kept = cap_pairs([*big, *small])
    big_kept = sorted(p.new_nodes for p in kept if p.pr == "big")
    # Sizes are 30..41; the ten largest are 32..41 (hand-worked), 30 and 31 are dropped.
    assert big_kept == list(range(32, 42))
    assert sum(p.pr == "small" for p in kept) == 3


def test_cap_ties_break_on_path_then_qualname_whatever_the_input_order():
    tied = [
        pair(pr="t", new="z.f", nodes=50, path="b/z.py"),
        pair(pr="t", new="a.f", nodes=50, path="b/a.py"),
        pair(pr="t", new="m.f", nodes=50, path="a/m.py"),
    ]
    for _ in range(5):
        random.shuffle(tied)
        # All three tie on nodes, so the cap of 2 keeps the two smallest paths:
        # a/m.py then b/a.py.
        assert [p.new_path for p in cap_pairs(tied, k=2)] == ["a/m.py", "b/a.py"]


def test_expand_pairs_each_new_member_with_its_highest_overlap_existing_partner():
    members = [
        member("n.one", new=True),
        member("n.two", new=True),
        member("o.low", new=False),
        member("o.high", new=False),
    ]
    overlaps = {("n.one", "o.low"): 0.5, ("n.one", "o.high"): 0.9}
    pairs, dropped = expand_a_firing(
        "9",
        "r/x",
        members,
        overlap=lambda n, o: overlaps.get((n.qualname, o.qualname), 0.0),
        exists_at_both=lambda m: True,
    )
    assert dropped == 0
    by_new = {p.new_qualname: p.existing_qualname for p in pairs}
    # n.one has a clear best partner; n.two ties at 0 overlap, so the smaller
    # (path, qualname) wins: o/high.py sorts before o/low.py.
    assert by_new == {"n.one": "o.high", "n.two": "o.high"}
    assert all(p.generators == ("A",) for p in pairs)


def test_expand_skips_a_partner_that_does_not_exist_at_both_and_counts_drops():
    members = [member("n.f", new=True), member("o.best", new=False), member("o.ok", new=False)]
    overlap = {"o.best": 0.9, "o.ok": 0.1}
    # The best partner by overlap is gone at head: the fixture must reach that branch.
    assert overlap["o.best"] > overlap["o.ok"]
    pairs, dropped = expand_a_firing(
        "9",
        "r/x",
        members,
        overlap=lambda n, o: overlap[o.qualname],
        exists_at_both=lambda m: m.qualname != "o.best",
    )
    assert [p.existing_qualname for p in pairs] == ["o.ok"] and dropped == 0
    none, dropped = expand_a_firing(
        "9", "r/x", members, overlap=lambda n, o: 0.0, exists_at_both=lambda m: False
    )
    assert none == [] and dropped == 1  # one new member, no partner: dropped, never scored


def test_calibrate_picks_the_largest_similarity_whose_mean_meets_the_target():
    """Hand-worked on three PRs, target 1.0 pair per PR (mean over all three, zeros count).

    t=0.9: counts 1,0,0 -> 1/3.  t=0.85: 1,1,0 -> 2/3.  t=0.8: 2,1,0 -> 3/3 = 1.0.
    The first (largest) t that reaches 1.0 is 0.8.
    """
    scores = {"p1": [0.9, 0.8, 0.7], "p2": [0.85], "p3": []}
    assert calibrate_cutoff(scores, target=1.0) == 0.8


def test_calibrate_cap_limits_a_pr_and_a_missed_target_keeps_every_candidate():
    """With k=1 a PR counts once however many pass: t=0.7 gives 1,1,0 -> 2/3 < 1.0."""
    scores = {"p1": [0.9, 0.8, 0.7], "p2": [0.85], "p3": []}
    assert calibrate_cutoff(scores, target=1.0, k=1) == 0.7  # the lowest observed


def test_calibrate_includes_every_pair_tied_at_the_cutoff():
    """One PR with 0.8, 0.8, 0.5 and target 2.0: t=0.8 admits both tied pairs, mean 2."""
    assert calibrate_cutoff({"p": [0.8, 0.8, 0.5]}, target=2.0) == 0.8


@pytest.mark.parametrize("scores", [{}, {"p": []}])
def test_calibrate_refuses_when_there_is_nothing_to_match(scores):
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        calibrate_cutoff(scores, target=1.0)


def test_pool_merges_a_pair_both_generators_found_and_keeps_the_rest():
    a = [pair(new="n.f", old="o.f", gens=("A",)), pair(new="n.g", old="o.g", gens=("A",))]
    b = [pair(new="n.f", old="o.f", gens=("B",), sim=0.91), pair(new="n.h", old="o.h", gens=("B",))]
    assert {p.pair_id for p in a} & {p.pair_id for p in b}  # one pair is in both
    pooled = pool_pairs(a, b)
    by_id = {p.pair_id: p for p in pooled}
    assert len(pooled) == 3
    assert by_id["1|n.f|o.f"].generators == ("A", "B")
    assert by_id["1|n.f|o.f"].similarity == 0.91
    assert by_id["1|n.g|o.g"].generators == ("A",)
    assert [p.pair_id for p in pooled] == sorted(by_id)
E

"""Labels in, pre-registered verdict out, for #587.

Expected values are worked by hand. Fixtures assert they reach the branch (an exact-tier
pair that is TRUE, a unit both generators found, an interval that straddles) before the
outcome is asserted, so a drifting fixture cannot quietly stop testing.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

# bench/ is not a package; append it (not insert(0)) so its generic module names cannot
# shadow stdlib/installed imports, mirroring tests/test_diff_duplicates_score.py.
sys.path.append(str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "bench"))

import embedding_oracle_score as sc  # ty: ignore[unresolved-import]  (added to sys.path above)
from embedding_oracle_pairs import Pair  # ty: ignore[unresolved-import]  (same)


def pair(pr, new, old, gens, *, repo=None, exact=False) -> Pair:
    return Pair(
        pr=pr,
        repo=repo or f"r/{pr}",
        new_path=f"{new}.py",
        new_qualname=new,
        new_nodes=40,
        new_shape="s" if exact else "a",
        existing_path=f"{old}.py",
        existing_qualname=old,
        existing_shape="s" if exact else "b",
        generators=gens,
    )


def test_resolve_labels_is_strict_and_drops_unscorable():
    a = {"p1": "TRUE", "p2": "TRUE", "p3": "FALSE", "p4": "UNSCORABLE", "p5": "TRUE"}
    b = {"p1": "TRUE", "p2": "FALSE", "p3": "FALSE", "p4": "TRUE", "p5": "UNSCORABLE"}
    # p1 both TRUE; p2 split (FALSE for the headline); p3 both FALSE; p4 and p5 dropped.
    assert sc.resolve_labels(a, b) == {"p1": True, "p2": False, "p3": False}


def test_resolve_labels_refuses_when_the_labelers_saw_different_pairs():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="different pairs"):
        sc.resolve_labels({"p1": "TRUE"}, {"p1": "TRUE", "p2": "TRUE"})


def test_wilson_matches_the_hand_worked_interval():
    """5 of 10: centre 0.5, half-width 0.2634 -> (0.2366, 0.7634). n=0 is the whole range."""
    low, high = sc.wilson(5, 10)
    assert low == pytest.approx(0.2366, abs=1e-3)
    assert high == pytest.approx(0.7634, abs=1e-3)
    assert sc.wilson(0, 0) == (0.0, 1.0)


def test_share_counts_units_by_generator_and_drops_exact_tier_before_forming_them():
    pairs = [
        pair("1", "n.a", "o.a", ("A",)),  # unit u1: only A found it
        pair("2", "n.b", "o.b", ("B",)),  # unit u2: only B found it
        pair("3", "n.c", "o.c", ("A",)),  # unit u3: A's pair...
        pair("3", "n.c", "o.d", ("B",)),  # ...and B's different pair, same unit: both
        pair("4", "n.e", "o.e", ("B",), exact=True),  # TRUE but exact-tier: excluded
        pair("5", "n.f", "o.f", ("B",)),  # labeled FALSE: not in the pool
    ]
    truth = {p.pair_id: True for p in pairs}
    truth[pairs[5].pair_id] = False
    assert pairs[4].exact_tier and truth[pairs[4].pair_id]  # the exclusion is exercised
    got = sc.share(pairs, truth)
    # Three TRUE units remain: only A 1, only B 1, both 1. The exact-tier unit is gone.
    assert (got.true_units, got.only_a, got.only_b, got.both) == (3, 1, 1, 1)
    assert got.point == pytest.approx(1 / 3)
    assert got.measurable is False  # 3 units is far below the floor of 40


def _pool(n_units: int, only_b: int, *, repos: int, prs: int) -> tuple[list[Pair], dict]:
    pairs = []
    for i in range(n_units):
        gens = ("B",) if i < only_b else ("A",)
        pr = str(i % prs)
        pairs.append(pair(pr, f"n.f{i}", f"o.f{i}", gens, repo=f"r/{i % repos}"))
    return pairs, {p.pair_id: True for p in pairs}


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("units", "repos", "prs", "measurable"),
    [
        (40, 15, 20, True),  # exactly on every floor
        (39, 15, 20, False),  # one unit short
        (40, 14, 20, False),  # one repository short
        (40, 15, 19, False),  # one PR short
    ],
)
def test_share_floors_are_exact(units, repos, prs, measurable):
    pairs, truth = _pool(units, 12, repos=repos, prs=prs)
    got = sc.share(pairs, truth)
    assert (got.repos, got.prs) == (min(repos, units), min(prs, units))  # fixture reaches it
    assert got.measurable is measurable
    assert got.only_b == 12  # 12 of the units are B-only by construction


def test_b_precision_is_over_every_labeled_b_pair_with_a_deterministic_interval():
    pairs = [
        pair("1", "n.a", "o.a", ("B",), repo="r/1"),
        pair("1", "n.b", "o.b", ("B",), repo="r/1"),
        pair("2", "n.c", "o.c", ("B",), repo="r/2"),
        pair("2", "n.d", "o.d", ("B", "A"), repo="r/2"),
        pair("3", "n.e", "o.e", ("A",), repo="r/3"),  # A only: not B's
    ]
    truth = {p.pair_id: t for p, t in zip(pairs, [True, False, True, False, True])}
    got = sc.b_precision(pairs, truth)
    # Four B pairs from two repos, two TRUE: 0.5.
    assert (got.scorable, got.repos, got.true, got.point) == (4, 2, 2, 0.5)
    assert 0.0 <= got.low <= 0.5 <= got.high <= 1.0
    assert sc.b_precision(pairs, truth) == got  # fixed seed, so the same interval twice


def test_b_precision_interval_collapses_when_every_pair_is_true():
    pairs = [pair(str(i), f"n.f{i}", f"o.f{i}", ("B",)) for i in range(6)]
    got = sc.b_precision(pairs, {p.pair_id: True for p in pairs})
    assert (got.point, got.low, got.high) == (1.0, 1.0, 1.0)


def prec(point, low, high, *, scorable=30, repos=10) -> sc.BPrecision:
    return sc.BPrecision(
        scorable=scorable, repos=repos, true=round(point * scorable), point=point, low=low, high=high
    )


def headline(point, low, high, *, measurable=True) -> sc.Share:
    return sc.Share(
        true_units=40,
        only_b=round(point * 40),
        only_a=0,
        both=0,
        repos=15,
        prs=20,
        measurable=measurable,
        point=point,
        low=low,
        high=high,
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("p", "s", "outcome"),
    [
        (prec(0.20, 0.10, 0.30), headline(0.5, 0.4, 0.6), "kill"),  # precision kill, interval clear
        (prec(0.35, 0.25, 0.45), headline(0.5, 0.4, 0.6), "null"),  # point < 0.40 but straddles
        (prec(0.70, 0.62, 0.80), headline(0.05, 0.02, 0.08), "kill"),  # share kill, clear
        (prec(0.70, 0.62, 0.80), headline(0.05, 0.02, 0.12), "null"),  # share straddles 0.10
        (prec(0.70, 0.62, 0.80), headline(0.50, 0.35, 0.65), "pass"),  # both bars, both clear
        (prec(0.70, 0.55, 0.80), headline(0.50, 0.35, 0.65), "null"),  # precision low straddles
        (prec(0.70, 0.62, 0.80), headline(0.40, 0.25, 0.55), "null"),  # share low straddles 0.30
        (prec(0.50, 0.40, 0.60), headline(0.20, 0.12, 0.30), "null"),  # between the bars
    ],
)
def test_verdict_applies_a_bar_only_when_the_interval_clears_it(p, s, outcome):
    assert sc.verdict(p, s).outcome == outcome


def test_a_straddling_precision_does_not_hide_a_definite_share_kill():
    """Kill is EITHER bar. Precision straddles 0.40, the share is clearly below 0.10."""
    got = sc.verdict(prec(0.35, 0.25, 0.45), headline(0.05, 0.02, 0.08))
    assert got.outcome == "kill"
    assert "share" in got.reason


def test_an_unmeasurable_share_can_never_pass_and_a_precision_kill_still_stands():
    unmeasurable = headline(0.5, 0.4, 0.6, measurable=False)
    assert sc.verdict(prec(0.70, 0.62, 0.80), unmeasurable).outcome == "not_measurable"
    assert sc.verdict(prec(0.20, 0.10, 0.30), unmeasurable).outcome == "kill"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(("scorable", "repos"), [(29, 10), (30, 9)])
def test_below_b_floors_nothing_is_decided_even_a_would_be_kill(scorable, repos):
    got = sc.verdict(prec(0.1, 0.0, 0.2, scorable=scorable, repos=repos), headline(0.5, 0.4, 0.6))
    assert got.outcome == "not_measurable"
E

## The one place the code decides something the prose left open

The pre-registration says a bar applies "only when the interval does not straddle it" and that kill is either bar. Read together: kill is either bar crossed with its whole interval on the kill side, so a straddling precision interval does not hide a definite share kill. ) -> tuple[list[Pair], int]:
    """One pair per new member, each with its best existing partner in the cluster.

    The partner is the existing member that exists at base AND head with the highest
    `overlap` with the new function; ties go to the smaller (path, qualname). A new
    member with no such partner is dropped, and the count of drops is returned so the
    caller reports it instead of scoring it clean.
    """
    old = [m for m in members if not m.is_new and exists_at_both(m)]
    new_members = [m for m in members if m.is_new]
    if not old:
        return [], len(new_members)
    pairs = [
        _pair(ref, new, min(old, key=lambda o: (-overlap(new, o), o.path, o.qualname)), ("A",))
        for new in new_members

    return pairs, 0

        repo=ref.repo,
        new_path=new.path,

    eligible new function in it (a PR with none maps to `[]`, so it counts as zero).
    Pairs tied at the cutoff are all included, and a PR contributes at most `k`. When
    no observed similarity reaches the target the lowest one is returned, which keeps
    every candidate; the caller records that this happened.
    """
    observed = _observed_descending(scores)
    for t in observed:
        if _mean_capped(scores, t, k) >= target:
            return t
    return observed[-1]


def _observed_descending(scores: Mapping[str, Sequence[float]]) -> list[float]:
    if not scores:
        raise ValueError("calibration subset is empty; there is no volume to match")
    observed = sorted({s for per_pr in scores.values() for s in per_pr}, reverse=True)
    if not observed:
        raise ValueError("calibration subset has no scored function; the cutoff is undefined")

"""Labels in, pre-registered verdict out, for #587.

The rules are the ones in `docs/research/EMBEDDING_ORACLE_RECALL.md`, each in one
small function so a boundary cannot drift:

- A pair is TRUE only if BOTH labelers say TRUE (strict); either labeler's UNSCORABLE
  drops it, never scores it FALSE.
- A (PR, new function) unit is TRUE if any labeled pair for it is TRUE; found by A or B
  by which generator emitted a TRUE pair; only by B if found by B and not by A.
- The headline share drops exact-tier pairs BEFORE units are formed.
- B precision is over all labeled B pairs; its interval is a bootstrap clustered by PR.
- A bar is applied to the point estimate only when its interval does not straddle it;
  otherwise the verdict is null.

Recall here is relative to the pooled set, never absolute.

archy:owns        BPrecision, OracleVerdict, Share, b_precision, resolve_labels, share,
                  verdict, wilson
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import random
from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence

from embedding_oracle_pairs import Pair  # ty: ignore[unresolved-import]  (bench/ is sys.path[0])
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict

PASS_PRECISION = 0.60
KILL_PRECISION = 0.40
PASS_SHARE = 0.30
KILL_SHARE = 0.10
MIN_B_SCORABLE = 30
MIN_B_REPOS = 10
MIN_TRUE_UNITS = 40
MIN_TRUE_REPOS = 15
MIN_TRUE_PRS = 20
BOOTSTRAP_RESAMPLES = 2000
BOOTSTRAP_SEED = 587
Z95 = 1.959963984540054


def resolve_labels(a: Mapping[str, str], b: Mapping[str, str]) -> dict[str, bool]:
    """Strict truth per pair id: both TRUE. A pair either labeler calls UNSCORABLE is absent.

    The labelers must have seen the same pairs; a mismatch is a refusal, since a pair one
    of them never saw would otherwise be silently scored as the other's answer.
    """
    if set(a) != set(b):
        raise ValueError(f"labelers saw different pairs: {len(set(a) ^ set(b))} ids differ")
    out: dict[str, bool] = {}
    for pid in sorted(a):
        if "UNSCORABLE" in (a[pid], b[pid]):
            continue
        out[pid] = a[pid] == "TRUE" and b[pid] == "TRUE"
    return out


def wilson(k: int, n: int) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """Wilson 95% interval for k of n; the whole unit interval when n is 0."""
    if n == 0:
        return 0.0, 1.0
    p = k / n
    denom = 1 + Z95**2 / n
    centre = (p + Z95**2 / (2 * n)) / denom
    half = Z95 * math.sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + Z95**2 / (4 * n**2)) / denom
    return max(0.0, centre - half), min(1.0, centre + half)


class Share(BaseModel):
    """The headline: how much of the strict TRUE pool only B found (exact-tier excluded)."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    true_units: int
    only_b: int
    only_a: int
    both: int
    repos: int
    prs: int
    measurable: bool
    point: float | None
    low: float | None
    high: float | None


def share(pairs: Sequence[Pair], truth: Mapping[str, bool]) -> Share:
    """Units from labeled, non-exact pairs; the floors decide whether the share is measurable."""
    labeled = [p for p in pairs if p.pair_id in truth and not p.exact_tier]
    units = _true_units([p for p in labeled if truth[p.pair_id]])
    n = len(units)
    only_b = _found_only_by(units, "B")
    only_a = _found_only_by(units, "A")
    repos = len(set().union(*(u.repos for u in units.values())))
    prs = len(set().union(*(u.prs for u in units.values())))
    low, high = _interval(only_b, n)
    return Share(
        true_units=n,
        only_b=only_b,
        only_a=only_a,
        both=n - only_b - only_a,
        repos=repos,
        prs=prs,
        measurable=n >= MIN_TRUE_UNITS and repos >= MIN_TRUE_REPOS and prs >= MIN_TRUE_PRS,
        point=_ratio(only_b, n),
        low=low,
        high=high,
    )


def _ratio(k: int, n: int) -> float | None:
    return k / n if n else None


def _interval(k: int, n: int) -> tuple[float | None, float | None]:
    return wilson(k, n) if n else (None, None)


def _found_only_by(units: Mapping[str, _Unit], generator: str) -> int:
    return sum(u.generators == {generator} for u in units.values())


class _Unit(BaseModel):
    generators: set[str]
    repos: set[str]
    prs: set[str]


def _true_units(true_pairs: Sequence[Pair]) -> dict[str, _Unit]:
    """One unit per (PR, new function), remembering which generators found it TRUE."""
    units: dict[str, _Unit] = {}
    for p in true_pairs:
        unit = units.setdefault(p.unit_id, _Unit(generators=set(), repos=set(), prs=set()))
        unit.generators.update(p.generators)
        unit.repos.add(p.repo)
        unit.prs.add(p.pr)
    return units


class BPrecision(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    scorable: int
    repos: int
    true: int
    point: float | None
    low: float | None
    high: float | None


def b_precision(pairs: Sequence[Pair], truth: Mapping[str, bool]) -> BPrecision:
    """Precision over every labeled B pair (exact tier included), with a PR-clustered interval."""
    scored = [p for p in pairs if "B" in p.generators and p.pair_id in truth]
    clusters: dict[str, list[bool]] = {}
    for p in scored:
        clusters.setdefault(p.pr, []).append(truth[p.pair_id])
    n = len(scored)
    k = sum(truth[p.pair_id] for p in scored)
    low, high = _cluster_bootstrap(list(clusters.values()))
    return BPrecision(
        scorable=n,
        repos=len({p.repo for p in scored}),
        true=k,
        point=k / n if n else None,
        low=low,
        high=high,
    )


def _cluster_bootstrap(clusters: Sequence[Sequence[bool]]) -> tuple[float | None, float | None]:
    """Percentile interval of precision, resampling whole PRs with a fixed seed."""
    if not clusters:
        return None, None
    rng = random.Random(BOOTSTRAP_SEED)
    stats: list[float] = []
    for _ in range(BOOTSTRAP_RESAMPLES):
        draw = [clusters[rng.randrange(len(clusters))] for _ in clusters]
        total = sum(len(c) for c in draw)
        if total:
            stats.append(sum(sum(c) for c in draw) / total)
    stats.sort()
    return stats[int(0.025 * len(stats))], stats[min(len(stats) - 1, int(0.975 * len(stats)))]


class OracleVerdict(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)

    outcome: str  # pass | kill | null | not_measurable
    reason: str


def _definite_kill(prec: BPrecision, headline: Share) -> str | None:
    """Why a bar is crossed with its whole interval on the kill side, or None."""
    if prec.high is not None and prec.high < KILL_PRECISION:
        return f"B precision {prec.point:.3f}, interval top {prec.high:.3f} < 0.40"
    return _share_kill(headline)


def _share_kill(headline: Share) -> str | None:
    if not headline.measurable or headline.high is None:
        return None
    if headline.high >= KILL_SHARE:
        return None
    return f"only-by-B share {headline.point:.3f}, interval top {headline.high:.3f} < 0.10"


def _definite_pass(prec: BPrecision, headline: Share) -> bool:
    """Both bars cleared with the whole interval above them, and the share measurable."""
    lows = (prec.low, headline.low)
    if not headline.measurable or any(v is None for v in lows):
        return False
    return (prec.low or 0.0) >= PASS_PRECISION and (headline.low or 0.0) >= PASS_SHARE


def verdict(prec: BPrecision, headline: Share) -> OracleVerdict:
    """The pre-registered rule.

    Not measurable below B's scorable floor. Kill is EITHER bar crossed with its whole
    interval on the kill side, and stands whether or not the other bar is measurable.
    Pass needs BOTH bars cleared with the whole interval above them, so an unmeasurable
    share can never pass. Anything else is null, or not measurable when the share's
    floor is what stopped a verdict. An interval that straddles a bar is never decided
    by its point estimate.
    """
    if prec.scorable < MIN_B_SCORABLE or prec.repos < MIN_B_REPOS:
        return OracleVerdict(
            outcome="not_measurable",
            reason=f"{prec.scorable} scorable B pairs from {prec.repos} repos; "
            f"need {MIN_B_SCORABLE} from {MIN_B_REPOS}",
        )
    killed = _definite_kill(prec, headline)
    if killed is not None:
        return OracleVerdict(outcome="kill", reason=killed)
    if _definite_pass(prec, headline):
        return OracleVerdict(
            outcome="pass", reason="precision and only-by-B share clear their bars"
        )
    if not headline.measurable:
        return OracleVerdict(
            outcome="not_measurable",
            reason="B precision is not a kill but the TRUE pool is below its floor, so no "
            "pass or share verdict is declared",
        )
    return OracleVerdict(outcome="null", reason="between the bars, or an interval straddles one")

name: github-closes-keyword

**`Closes #448, #455, #464` closes only #448.** GitHub honours a closing keyword
only where it directly precedes a number; the rest of a comma-separated list is
ignored, silently. Observed 2026-09-06 on archy PR #469: eight tickets listed,
one closed, seven left open with no warning anywhere.

Write `Closes #448, closes #455, closes #464`. PR #471 did that and all four
closed on merge.

**Why it matters beyond tidiness:** the PR body claims the tickets are done, so a
later reader trusts the list and the backlog quietly disagrees. Verify after any
multi-ticket merge rather than assuming, the same way [[verify-tests-by-mutation]]
treats a green suite. Related: [[github-rest-not-graphql]].

**Also (2026-11-09):** a negation does not help. PR #887 said "Does not close #870" and GitHub closed #870 on merge. Never write close/closes/fixes/resolves next to an issue number in a PR body unless the PR really finishes it; write "leaves #870 open" or "relates to #870" instead, and after merging check `gh api repos/:owner/:repo/issues/N --jq .state` for every ticket mentioned.

**Merge then delete the branch with `&&`, never `;` (2026-11-09).** `gh api -X PUT .../merge ...; gh api -X DELETE .../git/refs/heads/BRANCH` deleted the branch even though the merge was refused for conflicts, which closed PR #909 and GitHub then refused to reopen it ("branch was force-pushed or recreated"), costing a replacement PR. Always check the merge result before deleting: only delete when `.merged` is true.

**Never put backticks in an unquoted heredoc (2026-11-09).** `python3 - <<EOF ... \`code\` ... EOF` made the shell run every backtick span as a command and garbled a ticket comment. Write issue and PR text with a quoted heredoc (`<<'EOF'`) or from a file, then post it.

content.text:
Stage 2 is where the study's measurement actually happens, so its implications run past plumbing. Everything below about model internals and speed is from memory or rough estimates. I haven't checked the model cards, and verifying them would be the first step of stage 2.

## 1. Pinning the model revision

- **`trust_remote_code` means the pinned revision is code that runs on your machine.** The jina v2 code model needs it. As I remember it, those models' config pointed at a separate implementation repo (`jina-bert-implementation`) for the modeling code. If that's still true, pinning the model repo's commit doesn't pin the code that runs, and I'd have to pin and read that second repo too. This needs checking before anything loads.
- **Pins are more than one hash.** The model revision, the tokenizer revision, the `transformers` and `torch` versions, and any remote-code repo all matter. Token boundaries change the truncation point and the vector. The pre-registration says to run offline after the first fetch, so a later upstream push can't change a result mid-study.
- **Reproducibility has a shelf life.** If someone deletes or force-pushes the revision, the study can't be re-run. Recording the sha256 of the weight files in the addendum makes that detectable.
- **The sensitivity model is `cc-by-nc-4.0`.** It stays bench-only: no weights in the repo, and the cache is gitignored. Reporting numbers from it is fine, but nothing derived from it can ship in the product.

## 2. The content-hash cache

- **Cache keys have to match the pre-registration exactly.** That means content hash, model id, revision, truncation length and input normalization. Missing any one produces silent stale hits, which is the failure that looks like a result. The pre-registration also says the results quote the revision each cached row carries, not the one the harness intended.
- **Device and dtype are a gap in the pre-registration.** A Mac can run on CPU or on MPS, and the two give slightly different float32 vectors. The cutoff is a threshold on cosine similarity, so mixing vectors from both can flip a pair near the cutoff. The pre-registration's cache key doesn't include device. I'd freeze CPU and float32 before the pilot and state it in the addendum.
- **Reuse should be high, which helps cost.** Most functions don't change between a repo's PRs, so identical text embeds once. The cache is about 3 KB per function at 768 dimensions, so a million functions is about 3 GB. That fits on your disk (116 GB free).
- **Exact 1.0 pairs are legitimate.** Byte-identical functions in two files get cosine 1.0. They count toward calibration volume as pre-registered, and the exact-tier exclusion handles them in the headline share.

## 3. Cost and what the pilot decides

- **Large repos dominate.** Every base-commit function in a repo gets embedded for each PR whose base differs. A repo with tens of thousands of functions could take on the order of tens of minutes on CPU for the 161M model, and several times that for the 0.5B model. These are guesses. The pilot is where wall time gets measured, and the pre-registration fixes M from it.
- **The pilot's 7 measured PRs are a weak sample for this.** Collision-dropped repos in #548 were the large ones, so the pilot may understate embedding cost. The addendum has to say so. If the affordable M gives an expected TRUE pool under 40 labeled units, the pre-registration says to record "not measurable" before the run. That is a real possibility given A's 0.16 precision.
- **Failures are expected.** An 8k-token function can run out of memory and a load can fail. The pre-registration says a PR whose embedding run fails is dropped with its reason, never scored clean, and the ledger must carry that.

## 4. Ordering constraints that protect the result

- **Calibration comes first and is frozen in a commit.** The cutoff comes from the 40 calibration PRs only. Warming the cache for evaluation repos beforehand is harmless, but I shouldn't compute evaluation similarities or read evaluation candidates until the addendum with the cutoffs is committed.
- **The canary still has to pass before any real run.** A loop and a comprehension computing the same thing must be found by B and missed by A. That is the only direct check that this model, at this pin, sees Type-4 at all.

## Decisions I need from you

1. **Device:** CPU and float32 only (slow, reproducible) or allow MPS (faster, small numeric drift).
2. **Remote code:** is it acceptable to run the pinned jina remote code on your machine, after I read it? The alternative is a vendored copy of the modeling file I'd review and pin in the bench tree, which is more work.
3. **Sensitivity model:** run it now, or only after the primary result, since it can't change the verdict and roughly triples embedding time.

Want me to start by checking both model cards and the remote-code repo, so these answers rest on facts?
